When externalCalendarId is falsy, the find compares cal.externalId against undefined/null, which never matches, so the fallback always yields undefined — whereas the removed code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, a potentially valid calendar id. This is a verifiable dead-branch regression for legacy bookings lacking a stored externalCalendarId, breaking reschedule/cancel on Google Cal

adjudication.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent and deleteEvent, the fallback branch is `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. In that branch `externalCalendarId` is falsy by definition, so the `.find(...)` compares against `undefined`/`null` and will almost never match a real `externalId`, yielding `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` as `undefined`. This is a diff-introduced logic error vs the prior `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` behavior (now destinationCalendar is an array), and can cause updates/deletes to target no calendarId (or fall back incorrectly if later defaulted), breaking reschedule/cancel for cases without stored `externalCalendarId`.
